goal: Add src/slugify.js exporting slugify(text): lowercase the text, trim it, replace every run of characters that are not a-z or 0-9 with a single hyphen, and strip leading and trailing hyphens. Accented Latin letters are reduced to their base letter first ("Crème Brûlée" becomes "creme-brulee"). Add tests in test/slugify.test.js.

Add src/duration.js exporting parseDuration(text) that turns strings like "1h30m", "45s" or "2d4h" into a number of seconds. The input is one or more parts of <non-negative integer><unit> with units d, h, m, s, written in that order (d before h before m before s), each unit at most once, no spaces. Throw an Error for anything else: empty string, non-string input, unknown unit, a unit without a number, a number without a unit, units out of order, or a repeated unit. Add tests in test/duration.test.js.

Bug report: chunk([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], 2) in src/array.js returns [[1, 2], [3, 4]] but should return [[1, 2], [3, 4], [5]]: the last, shorter group is dropped. Fix it. Also make chunk throw a RangeError when size is not a positive integer. Add tests for both.

Rename the function sum in src/array.js to total. Keep sum exported as a deprecated alias that returns the same result (mark it with a @deprecated JSDoc tag). Update every internal caller in src/ to use total. Update the tests.

Add src/lru.js exporting a class LRUCache. new LRUCache(capacity) throws a RangeError unless capacity is a positive integer. Methods: get(key) returns the value or undefined and marks the key as most recently used; set(key, value) stores or updates the value, marks it most recently used and, when the cache holds more than capacity entries, evicts the least recently used one; has(key) returns a boolean and does not change recency; delete(key) removes the key and returns whether it existed. A size getter returns the number of entries. Add tests in test/lru.test.js.

Add a command line tool bin/wc.js. Running `node bin/wc.js <file>` reads the file as UTF-8 and prints one line: `<lines> <words> <chars>` followed by a newline, where lines is the number of \n characters, words is the number of runs of non-whitespace characters, and chars is the number of Unicode code points. With no argument, or if the file cannot be read, it prints an error message to stderr and exits with code 1. Put the counting in src/wc.js as an exported function count(text) returning { lines, words, chars }, and add tests.

Add POST /todos to the API in src/server.js. The body is JSON {"title": string}. The title is trimmed; it must be a non-empty string of at most 200 characters after trimming. On success respond 201 with the created todo {"id", "title", "done": false}; ids are one higher than the highest existing id (1 for an empty store). A missing or invalid title, or a body that is not valid JSON, gets 400 with {"error": "<message>"}. The new todo appears in GET /todos. Add tests.

Add DELETE /todos/:id to the API in src/server.js. If a todo with that id exists, remove it and respond 204 with an empty body. If the id is a positive integer but no todo has it, respond 404 with {"error": "<message>"}. If the id is not a positive integer (for example abc, 0, -1 or 1.5), respond 400 with {"error": "<message>"}. Add tests.

Add textstats/roman.py with to_roman(n) and from_roman(s). to_roman converts an int from 1 to 3999 to an uppercase Roman numeral (1994 -> "MCMXCIV") and raises ValueError for anything else, including bools, floats and out-of-range ints. from_roman converts a numeral back and accepts only canonical uppercase numerals in that range (the exact strings to_roman produces); anything else, such as "IIII", "IC", "mcm" or "", raises ValueError. Add tests in tests/test_roman.py.

Bug report: textstats.words.word_count gives wrong answers. word_count("hello   world") returns 4 and word_count("") returns 1. A word is a run of letters, digits and apostrophes, so "it's" is one word, "well-known" is two, and punctuation on its own ("--", "...") is not a word. Whitespace of any kind (spaces, tabs, newlines) separates words. Fix word_count and add tests.

Add coupon support to the shop. Put the coupon definitions in src/coupons.js: SAVE10 takes 10% off the subtotal; FLAT500 takes 500 cents off when the subtotal is at least 2000 cents (otherwise it gives no discount). Cart gets applyCoupon(code), which throws an Error for an unknown code; applying a coupon replaces any earlier one (one coupon per cart). Cart also gets coupon() returning the applied code or null, and discount() returning the discount in cents for the current subtotal, rounded half up to a whole cent and never more than the subtotal. placeOrder returns { id, lines, subtotal, discount, tax, total, coupon }: tax is computed on the discounted subtotal and total is subtotal - discount + tax; orders without a coupon have discount 0 and coupon null. salesReport adds `discounts` (the sum of order discounts) and `byCoupon` (number of orders per coupon code, {} when none). Add tests.

Bug report from accounting: the sales report undercounts units. A customer added 2 mugs to their cart, then added 1 more mug before checking out, and salesReport shows MUG-01: 1 instead of 3. The order total was too low as well. Find the real cause and fix it, and add a regression test.

The shop keeps its state in module-level variables (stock in src/catalog.js, the order list and next order id in src/orders.js), so two shops, or two tests, share stock and order ids. Add src/shop.js exporting createShop(products) that returns an independent shop object: { getProduct(sku), listProducts(), newCart(), placeOrder(cart), listOrders(), salesReport() }. products is optional and has the same shape as the standard catalog ({ SKU: { name, price, stock } }); when omitted, the shop starts from a fresh copy of the standard catalog. Each shop has its own stock, its own orders and its own order ids starting at 1, and carts from newCart() use that shop's products. Keep the existing exports of src/index.js working as before, acting on one default shop. Add tests.

Add filtering and pagination to GET /todos. Optional query parameters: done=true or done=false filters by the done flag; limit (an integer from 1 to 100) and offset (an integer of 0 or more, default 0) select a page of the filtered list. Todos are always returned in ascending id order, even if the store was seeded in another order. The body stays a JSON array, and every GET /todos response sets the X-Total-Count header to the number of todos matching the filter before pagination. Any invalid value (done not true/false, limit or offset not an integer or out of range) or any unknown query parameter gets 400 with {"error": "<message>"}. Add tests.

Add src/sort.js exporting sortBy(items, spec). spec is a comma-separated list of property names, each optionally followed by :asc or :desc (default asc), for example "lastName,age:desc". Return a new array sorted by the first key, ties broken by the next key and so on; items equal on every key keep their original relative order, and the input array is not modified. Numbers compare numerically. Strings compare case-insensitively and numeric-aware, so "file2" comes before "file10" and "a" equals "A". null and undefined values always sort last, whatever the direction. Throw an Error for an empty spec or a direction other than asc or desc. Add tests.

Add textstats/csvparse.py with parse_csv(text) returning a list of rows, each a list of strings, following RFC 4180, without using the csv module. Fields are separated by commas and records by \n or \r\n. A field may be enclosed in double quotes; inside quotes, two double quotes stand for one, and commas and line breaks are part of the field. Fields are returned exactly as written (no trimming). A line break at the very end of the text does not create an extra row, an empty line elsewhere is a row with one empty field, and empty text gives []. Raise ValueError for a quote that is never closed, for a double quote inside an unquoted field, and for characters after a closing quote other than a comma or a line break. Add tests in tests/test_csvparse.py.

Add a package semver (directory semver/) with func Valid(v string) bool and func Compare(a, b string) (int, error) implementing Semantic Versioning 2.0.0. A version is MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with an optional -prerelease and an optional +build, with no leading "v". Numeric identifiers (the three core numbers and numeric prerelease identifiers) must not have leading zeros; identifiers use only [0-9A-Za-z-] and must not be empty. Compare returns -1, 0 or 1 by precedence: core numbers compared numerically; a version with a prerelease is lower than the same version without one; prerelease identifiers are compared left to right, numeric ones numerically, alphanumeric ones in ASCII order, numeric ones lower than alphanumeric ones, and when all shared identifiers are equal the shorter list is lower; build metadata is ignored. Compare returns an error if either version is invalid. Add tests.

Replace the open/closed ticket status with a workflow. Statuses are open, in_progress, resolved and closed. Allowed transitions: open -> in_progress; in_progress -> open or resolved; resolved -> open or closed; closed -> open. Moving to in_progress requires the ticket to have an assignee. Add a service method transition(id, to, by), where by is the name of the person making the change (same format rules as an assignee). A transition that is not allowed, or moving to in_progress without an assignee, throws ConflictError; an unknown status or an invalid or missing by throws ValidationError; an unknown id throws NotFoundError. Every successful transition appends { from, to, by, at } to the ticket's history, where at is the clock time as an ISO string; add history(id) returning that list, oldest first ([] for a ticket without transitions). list({ status }) accepts the four statuses. Remove close() and the POST /tickets/:id/close route; instead add POST /tickets/:id/transitions with body { to, by } (200 with the updated ticket) and GET /tickets/:id/history (200 with the list), with errors mapped to 400, 404 and 409 as elsewhere. GET /tickets?status=in_progress must work. Update the existing tests and add new ones.

Add SLA due dates. Business hours are Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 17:00 UTC (17:00 itself is outside). Add src/sla.js exporting SLA_HOURS = { urgent: 4, high: 8, normal: 24, low: 40 } and addBusinessHours(start, hours), which returns a new Date that is `hours` business hours (a non-negative integer) after the Date `start`, without modifying start. Counting only runs during business hours: if start is outside them, counting begins at the next opening, so adding 0 hours to a time on a Saturday gives the following Monday 09:00, and a deadline that falls exactly at 17:00 stays at 17:00. Every ticket gets dueAt, an ISO string equal to addBusinessHours(createdAt, SLA_HOURS[priority]). Add a service method setPriority(id, priority) that validates the priority and recomputes dueAt from createdAt; PATCH /tickets/:id accepts priority as well as assignee (either or both; invalid values give 400). A ticket is overdue when its status is open and its dueAt is before the clock's current time. list() accepts overdue: true or false, and GET /tickets accepts ?overdue=true or ?overdue=false (any other value gives 400). Update the existing tests and add new ones.

Add bulk import: POST /tickets/import with a CSV body and Content-Type text/csv (parameters such as charset are allowed). The first line is a header naming the columns, in any order: title (required), priority and assignee (optional); any other column name is an error. Lines end with 
 or 
 and a trailing line break is ignored. Fields are separated by commas and may be enclosed in double quotes, in which case they may contain commas and "" stands for one double quote. An empty priority or assignee means the same default as when creating a ticket. Every row is validated with the same rules as creating a ticket. If any row is invalid, create nothing and respond 422 with { errors: [{ row, error }] } listing every invalid row, where row is the 1-based number of the data row (the header is not counted). Rows whose title matches an existing ticket's title or an earlier row's title, ignoring case and surrounding spaces, are skipped (they are not errors). Otherwise create the remaining rows in file order and respond 201 with { created: [ids], skipped: <number of skipped rows> }. A content type other than text/csv, a missing title column or an unknown column gets 400. Put the CSV parsing in its own module and the import rules in the service, and add tests.

Add partial refunds. Add refund(orderId, sku, qty) to src/orders.js and export it from src/index.js. It refunds qty units of one line of an order: the order must exist, the order must have a line for that sku, qty must be a positive integer, and the total refunded units of a line can never exceed the units bought on it; any violation throws an Error. Refunded units go back into stock. The amount of a refund is unitPrice * qty plus a share of the order's tax: round half up of order.tax * (unitPrice * qty) / order.subtotal, except that when this refund makes every unit of the whole order refunded, the tax share is all of the order's tax not yet refunded, so a fully refunded order gives back exactly its total. Every order gets refunds: [{ sku, qty, amount }] and refunded (the sum of the amounts), which are [] and 0 for an order without refunds. refund returns the new { sku, qty, amount } entry. salesReport adds refunds (the sum of all refunded amounts) and netRevenue (revenue minus refunds), and its bySku counts net units (bought minus refunded). Add tests.

difficulty: series: 3 goals in a row on one repo (tags, tag filter, tag stats)
goals: Add tags to tickets. A ticket has tags, an array of strings; a valid tag is 1 to 20 characters of lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter. Tags given by callers are trimmed and lower-cased before they are checked. create() accepts an optional tags array (default []): duplicates are dropped keeping the first occurrence, at most 10 tags, and an invalid tag or a tags value that is not an array is a ValidationError. Add service methods addTag(id, tag), which adds the normalized tag if it is not there yet (adding one that is there is not an error, but an 11th tag is), and removeTag(id, tag), which removes it if present (removing a missing tag is not an error). Both validate the tag and throw NotFoundError for an unknown ticket. Over HTTP: POST /tickets accepts tags; POST /tickets/:id/tags with body { tag } returns 200 and the ticket; DELETE /tickets/:id/tags/:tag returns 200 and the ticket. Errors keep the existing statuses and { error } body. Update the README and the tests.

Let tickets be filtered by tag. list() accepts tag (normalized like stored tags: trimmed and lower-cased; an invalid tag is a ValidationError) and combines it with the status and assignee filters. GET /tickets accepts ?tag=. Tickets stored before tags existed have no tags field: treat them as having no tags, and return them with tags: [] from get() and list(). Update the README and the tests.

Add tag statistics. A service method tagStats() returns [{ tag, open, total }] for every tag on any ticket, where total is the number of tickets with that tag and open the number of those whose status is open, sorted by total descending and then by tag name ascending. GET /tags returns that list. Update the README and the tests.

difficulty: series: 3 goals in a row on one repo (create, update/delete, filters)
goals: Add POST /todos: the JSON body has a title (a string, trimmed, 1 to 100 characters); create the todo with the next id (one more than the highest id ever used in this server, starting after the seeded todos) and done false, and respond 201 with it. A missing, empty or too long title, a body that is not valid JSON or not a JSON object gives 400 with the usual { error } body. Add tests.

Add PATCH /todos/:id with a JSON body containing title and/or done (title validated as for POST, done must be a boolean; a body with neither is invalid) that responds 200 with the updated todo, and DELETE /todos/:id that responds 204 with an empty body. An id that is not a positive integer gives 400, an unknown todo 404, an invalid body 400, all with the usual { error } body, and a rejected update changes nothing. Ids of deleted todos are never reused. Add tests.

Let GET /todos filter: ?done=true or ?done=false keeps only todos with that done value (any other value gives 400), and ?q=text keeps todos whose title contains the trimmed text, ignoring case (an empty q does not filter). The filters can be combined, and the list stays in id order. Add tests.

difficulty: greenfield: an empty repo, then a scaffold goal and a feature goal
goals: Set up a Node.js 22 project in this empty repository: a package.json with "type": "module", no dependencies, and a "test" script that runs `node --test`; a src/ folder for the code; a test/ folder with one passing test; a .gitignore for node_modules/; and a README that says how to run the tests.

Add src/inventory.js exporting a class Inventory and an error class InsufficientStockError (extends Error, name "InsufficientStockError", with properties sku, requested and available). A SKU is trimmed and upper-cased, and must then be 3 to 20 characters of A-Z, 0-9 and hyphens, else a TypeError (also for non-strings). Quantities must be positive integers, else a RangeError. add(sku, qty) adds to the stock and returns the new quantity. remove(sku, qty) returns what is left; asking for more than is in stock (also for an unknown SKU, which has 0) throws InsufficientStockError and changes nothing; a SKU whose stock reaches 0 is dropped. quantity(sku) returns the stock, 0 if unknown. list() returns copies, [{ sku, qty }] sorted by SKU. total() returns the sum of all stock. Add tests in test/inventory.test.js.

difficulty: multi-round: a visible API contract (route registry, docs table, test names) that a first attempt tends to miss
goal: Add PATCH /todos/:id to the API. The body is JSON with "title" and/or "done": a title is trimmed and must then be 1 to 200 characters; done must be a boolean. At least one of the two is required. Respond 200 with the updated todo, 404 with {"error"} for an unknown id, and 400 with {"error"} for invalid JSON, a body without either field, or an invalid value, changing nothing. Add tests.

difficulty: multi-round: house rules checked by npm run lint (JSDoc tags, no console, a test per module) that a first attempt tends to miss
goal: Add src/retry.js exporting an async function retry(fn, options) that calls fn(attempt) (attempt counts from 1; fn may be sync or async) until it succeeds and returns its result. Options: attempts (total tries, default 3, a positive integer, else RangeError), delayMs (wait before the second try, default 100, a number >= 0, else RangeError), factor (each later wait is multiplied by it, default 2) and shouldRetry(err) (return false to rethrow at once; default retries every error). After the last attempt, throw its error. A non-function fn is a TypeError. Add tests.

difficulty: visual: three separate causes of sideways scroll on phones and an unreadable dark-mode header, graded in a browser
goal: Users report two bugs on /dashboard. On phones (375px wide) the page scrolls sideways and the Export CSV button is cut off at the right edge. In dark mode the table's column headers cannot be read. Fix both. On a desktop in light mode the page must look as it does now: the toolbar buttons on one row, the four stats on one row, and the table headers keep their light gray background.

difficulty: visual: responsive cards and a site-wide dark theme, graded in a browser
goal: Add a /pricing page (public/pricing.html) with three plan cards, Free, Pro and Team: side by side on desktop, stacked in one column on phones, and never wider than the screen. Give each card the class "plan" and put the plan's name in an h2 inside it. Add a dark theme for the whole site that follows the system setting (prefers-color-scheme), with readable text. Link Pricing from the header nav on every page.
